newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Senate passes gambling regulation measure.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Senate passes gambling regulation measure.

text.p: California's Senate on Wednesday unanimously approved a bill that would help the state regulate card rooms and other legal gambling operations.
The Senate voted 37-to-0 for Senate Bill 8, which now moves to the Assembly for review.
The bill, by Senate President Bill Lockyer, would create a Division of Gambling Control within the state's Department of Justice to regulate legal gambling.
The bill would also establish the California Gambling Control Board to hear appeals of decisions made by the Division of Gambling Control.
"It is a sensible plan to provide needed regulation, but which avoids the creation of an unnecessary new bureaucracy," Lockyer, a Democrat, said in a statement.
The Gambling Control Board would be made up of three members appointed by the governor and confirmed by the state Senate, according to the bill.
The measure would appropriate $5.4 million in funding, which would come from license fees paid by card rooms and other legal gambling establishments, Lockyer's office said.
